handbookNote: New Jersey Real Estate Broker license exam. This is a genuinely NEW track for this site -- New Jersey previously had no broker-tier track at all, only nj_real_estate (salesperson). Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the New Jersey Real Estate Commission (NJREC). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly fetching and reading (via pdftotext against the raw PDF, after WebFetch's own summarizer flagged the file as an unreadable Excel-to-PDF export) PSI's own official 'State of New Jersey Real Estate Salesperson, Broker and Instructor Examination -- Candidate Information Bulletin' (copyright 2020 by PSI Services LLC, effective 9/21/2020, distributed via www.psiexams.com/njre). This single document supplied BOTH the exam mechanics AND the full real content outline used to size this bank -- not a third-party test-prep summary. Exam Summary Table, quoted directly from the bulletin: Broker exam = 115 questions (120 points), 70% passing (84 correct points), 4-hour time limit; a footnoted hedge on the same table states 'National broker exams include questions that are scored up to two points each,' which this bank discloses honestly rather than silently treating all 115 items as worth 1 point apiece. A small number of unscored 'experimental' questions (the bulletin says 5 to 10) may also appear and are already included in the 115 -- not additional. Broker eligibility (PRIMARY-CONFIRMED from the same bulletin): 3 years' full-time salesperson experience, approved by NJREC, plus 150 hours of broker prelicensure education completed in a fixed sequence -- the 90-hour general course first, then the two 30-hour courses (ethics/agency, and office management) -- after which a candidate applies for experience approval ($25 fee) and, once approved, receives a Certificate of Examination Eligibility from NJREC that must be presented (hard copy only, digital not accepted) at every sitting. CONTENT OUTLINE -- the bulletin states the exam is a National portion plus a New Jersey state-specific portion, not separately scored/reported, and PRIMARY-CONFIRMS the item counts: for Broker, the National portion is 75 of the 115 items and the New Jersey portion is 40 of the 115 items (110-total Salesperson exam = 80 national + 30 state, confirming the analogous split pattern referenced in this build's brief). National portion weighting, quoted verbatim from the bulletin's own content-outline percentages (of the 75-item national portion, Broker column): Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls and Regulations 5%, Valuation and Market Analysis 7%, Financing 8%, General Principles of Agency 11%, Property Disclosures 7%, Contracts 18% (by far the largest single national topic), Leasing and Property Management 5%, Transfer of Title 7%, Practice of Real Estate 14%, Real Estate Calculations 8% -- summing to exactly 100% of the national portion, independently re-verified by hand this session. New Jersey state-specific portion, quoted verbatim as item counts (of the 40-item state portion, Broker column): Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission 3 items (Maintenance of Records; Sanctions -- fines, license suspension/revocation); Licensing Requirements 4 items (Activities Requiring a License; Types of Licenses); Statutes and Rules Governing Licensee Activities 30 items (the largest state bucket, covering Advertising, Broker/Salesperson Relationships, Commissions and Required Accounting, Agency/Conflicts of Interest/Disclosure Requirements, Contracts and Other Documents, Trust Fund Requirements, Listings and Content of Listing Agreements, Place of Business, Records including Escrow Account Bookkeeping, Inducements, Offering Buyer Rebates, Responsibility to Public and Other Licensees, and 'Other Laws and Regulations' explicitly naming the Farmland Reassessment Act, Pinelands Protection Act of 1979, Realty Transfer Fee, Mount Laurel Requirements, zoning/building codes, Municipal Land Use Law, real estate transfer tax, Truth in Renting Act, and Freshwater Wetlands Protection Act of 1987); Additional Requirements 3 items (New Jersey Real Estate Sales Full Disclosure Act, New Jersey Law Against Discrimination, Real Estate Guaranty Fund, New Jersey Real Estate Time Share Act). This bank's bucket sizing is directly proportional to these real, PSI-published weights (each national bucket's question count = its published % x 75/115 of the exam; each NJ bucket's question count = its published item-count/115 of the exam), not an even split, per the build's explicit sizing rule -- verified by hand this session against the bulletin's own numbers before drafting began. The 30-item 'Statutes and Rules' state bucket was split across four question-bank files by natural subtopic grouping (broker-salesperson relationships/commissions/trust accounting; agency disclosure/advertising/listings/place of business; inducements/rebates/responsibility-to-public/discipline; and the named NJ land-use/environmental/tax acts) since a single 30-item bucket covers too many distinct legal topics to usefully group as one exam-app 'topic' label. Real New Jersey statute/regulation facts independently verified this session (via law.justia.com, law.cornell.edu, and current secondary reporting cross-checked against those primary texts) and used as pinpoint citations: N.J.S.A. 45:15-1 et seq. (NJ Real Estate License Act); 45:15-3 (license required before bringing legal action for commission); 45:15-9 (license types -- broker, broker-salesperson, salesperson; a broker-salesperson is broker-qualified but licensed/supervised under another broker, exactly like a standard salesperson for supervisory purposes; only a licensed broker may employ/supervise); 45:15-17 (Commission investigation/discipline authority and grounds); 45:15-34 et seq. (Real Estate Guaranty Fund, funded from a portion of license fees, compensating the public for uncollectible judgments against licensees for fraud/misrepresentation/conversion, capped at $20,000 per transaction since P.L.1993, c.51 raised it from the original $10,000 cap for later-accruing claims); N.J.A.C. 11:5-5.1 (special accounts for funds of others -- deposit/trust monies must be placed in a dedicated trust account within 5 business days of receipt, no commingling with the broker's own operating funds); N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq. (NJ Law Against Discrimination, LAD -- protected classes include the federal FHA's classes plus NJ additions such as gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, marital/familial status, and, since a 2018 amendment, 'source of lawful income' as a housing-specific protected class, going further than federal law; enforced by the Division on Civil Rights); N.J.S.A. 54:4-23.1 et seq. (Farmland Assessment Act, commonly called the Farmland Reassessment Act in NJREC's own course-syllabus language -- qualifying active agricultural/horticultural acreage assessed at agricultural rather than fair-market value, subject to a rollback tax if use changes); N.J.S.A. 13:18A-1 et seq. (Pinelands Protection Act of 1979, creating the NJ Pinelands Commission and its comprehensive management plan for the ~1-million-acre Pinelands National Reserve); N.J.S.A. 13:9B-1 et seq. (Freshwater Wetlands Protection Act of 1987, NJDEP-administered, permit and buffer/transition-area requirements graduated by wetland resource-value classification); N.J.S.A. 40:55D-1 et seq. (Municipal Land Use Law -- planning boards, zoning boards of adjustment, municipal master plans, the 'c' bulk/dimensional variance vs. 'd' use-variance framework); N.J.S.A. 52:27D-301 et seq. (state Fair Housing Act codifying the Mount Laurel I/II affordable-housing obligation, historically administered through COAH and now largely court-supervised); N.J.S.A. 46:8-43 et seq. (Truth in Renting Act -- landlords must furnish tenants the state's Truth-in-Renting statement); the Realty Transfer Fee and its 2025 'mansion tax' reform (effective July 10, 2025, a tiered 1%-3.5% fee on residential transfers over $1,000,000 in $500K bands, with the SELLER now responsible for payment -- a genuine, recent legislative change from the prior buyer-pays convention, flagged in-content as a 2025 reform so users aren't misled by older buyer-pays material still circulating); and New Jersey's real Consumer Information Statement (CIS) agency-disclosure practice (delivery, not signature, required at first substantive contact, disclosing five relationship types -- seller's agent, buyer's agent, disclosed dual agent, designated agent, transaction broker/facilitator). Two NJ-specific acts named in the bulletin's own outline -- the New Jersey Real Estate Sales Full Disclosure Act and the New Jersey Real Estate Time Share Act -- are real, NJREC-administered laws (subdivided-land purchaser disclosure/registration, and timeshare-interest registration/disclosure, respectively) but their exact current N.J.S.A. section ranges were not independently pinpoint-verified against primary text this session; content on these two acts is deliberately hedged in-bank ('hedge: well-corroborated NJ practice/statute, exact section not independently pinpoint-verified this session') rather than assigned a guessed section number, consistent with this project's grounding standard. Standard national real-estate/appraisal/finance/contract-law/math content not tied to a New Jersey statute (property ownership, land use theory, valuation approaches, financing/underwriting mechanics, general agency and contract doctrine, federal fair housing/ADA, federal lead-paint disclosure, deed types, title/escrow/closing mechanics, and real estate calculations) is flagged 'hedge: standard real estate principle (national content outline)' or 'PSI national content outline: <topic>' throughout, per this project's standard for generic/national content never presented as a pinpoint state citation. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate track rate, consistent with ny_re_broker.json, ga_re_broker.json, pa_re_broker.json, ca_re_broker.json, fl_re_broker.json, oh_re_broker.json, tx_re_broker.json, and mi_re_broker.json. This 507-question initial bank was drafted across five parallel content-authoring passes (grouped by national-portion topics and NJ-specific-statute topics respectively), each pass instructed to draft every question with the correct answer as choice_a, then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_nj_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all questions in file order, not manual). All 507 draft questions passed an automated schema/weight-range/distinct-choice validation pass before rotation, and were run through this project's standard Jaccard-similarity dedup check (scripts/build-track-batch.js) to remove any exact or near-duplicate items before loading. POST-BUILD SPOT-CHECK (2026-09-02): 2 topics (Land Use Controls & Regulations, Leasing & Property Management) were checked for the target-anchoring bug documented in mo_re_broker.json and backfilled: 507->535 (4.65:1). FULL BACKFILL OF ALL REMAINING TOPICS (2026-09-02, per explicit user request to finish NJ/AZ's unchecked topics before closing out the N14 campaign): all 15 remaining topics were de-rotated, relaunched with no-ceiling prompts, and re-checked -- every single topic had genuine additional real content, several substantially so: Property Ownership 33->56, Valuation 23->38, Financing 26->47, General Principles of Agency 36->51, Property Disclosures 23->35, Contracts 59->101 (the largest single addition -- 42 new questions on contract-validity doctrines, conditions vs. covenants, discharge doctrines, and a full lease/purchase-contract subtopic that had been entirely absent), Transfer of Title 25->40, Practice of Real Estate 44->61, Real Estate Calculations 26->34, NJREC Duties & Licensing 30->44 (net, after removing 8 cross-bucket near-duplicates -- see below; gross addition was +22, drawing on previously-untested lettered grounds a-t of N.J.S.A. 45:15-17 and reinstatement-tier details of 45:15-9), Broker-Salesperson Relationships 37->48 (discovered an entirely new, real, on-point regulation -- N.J.A.C. 11:5-4.1, governing commission payment timing/accounting to salespersons and referral agents -- that the original build never found), Agency Disclosure/Advertising/Listings 36->69 (the single largest relative discovery of this backfill round -- found P.L.2024 c.32, New Jersey's 2024 statutory overhaul of real estate agency law codified at N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.86 through 45:15-16.101, which the original build had entirely missed and instead covered with 36 generically-hedged, non-pinpoint-cited questions), Inducements/Rebates/Discipline 30->48, NJ Land Use/Environmental/Tax Statutes 30->48, Additional NJ Requirements 14->17 (also resolved both of the original build's deliberately-hedged citations to real pinpoint sections -- the Real Estate Sales Full Disclosure Act at N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.27 et seq., and the New Jersey Real Estate Timeshare Act at 45:15-16.50 et seq.). A cross-bucket dedup check after this round found 8 genuine near-duplicates between NJREC Duties & Licensing and Inducements/Rebates/Discipline (both independently drew on the same lettered subsections of N.J.S.A. 45:15-17 -- (i), (k), (m), (p), (q), (s) -- with near-identical question framing), all 8 removed from NJREC Duties & Licensing and kept in Inducements/Rebates/Discipline as the more natural topical home for discipline-grounds content; a handful of other same-citation pairs (45:15-9, remaining 45:15-17 subsections, and generic Fair Housing Act/ADA citations shared between Leasing/Property Management and Practice of Real Estate) were individually inspected and confirmed to test genuinely distinct facts, not duplicates. Two backfill agents (General Principles of Agency, Contracts) and two more (Property Disclosures partial, Practice of Real Estate) hit a transient server error mid-response on first attempt; Property Disclosures had already written 12 of its questions before failing and that partial work was kept, while the other three were cleanly relaunched from scratch and succeeded. FINAL: 800 questions (up from 535) -- a 6.96:1 pool ratio, fully reloaded into D1 (535 old rows deleted, 800 new rows inserted, verified by count).
